newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary rate hike will not affect budget - ministry.
newsitem.headline: Hungary rate hike will not affect budget - ministry.

text.p: The National Bank of Hungary's (NBH) surprise rate hike announced earlier this week will not substantially increase the debt service expenditures of the state budget, the Finance Ministry said on Friday.
"The rate hike will stabilise interest rates temporarily, but will not affect state budget expenditures substantially," Deputy Secretary of State Csaba Laszlo told Reuters.

The NBH raised the interest rate of its six-month deposit facility by 0.25 percentage points to 21.00 percent on Monday, shocking the markets which had expected the continuation of a one year long trend of declining interest rates and inflation.
The NBH said its move was aimed at maintaining real interest levels so as to protect savings.

Analysts welcomed the NBH move and said inflation was likely to move a little upward in March and April and may rise slightly further or stabilise by the end of the third quarter of the year, due to energy and food price rises.
"Inflation may be higher in March and April," Laszlo said, adding that this would not change the underlying falling trend.
"We expect interest rates to go down in line with declining inflation," he said.

The Finance Ministry and the NBH expects inflation to drop to some 17 percent by December from 18.9 percent in January, while the forecasts of 15 analysts for December 1997 in a recent Reuters survey averaged at 18.39 percent.

Yields on government securities rose slightly on the secondary market following the NBH rate hike, but turnover slumped as buyers demanded sunstantially higher yields with the supply side hesitating to sell and suffer losses.
Traders were uncertain whether the NBH planned to keep its interest rates at current levels for the longer term.

"The pessimistic version (for sellers) is that the NBH will keep its interest rates (at the current level) for as much as two months," a trader said earlier this week. "At that point even those who have not sold so far may do so."
Analysts said the NBH interest rate hike may create some tension between the central bank and the Government Debt Management Agency, as it may increase the state budget debt financing burden.
